chapter: Trummy Young's band, 52nd Street and the Navy
title: First night in the barracks and the officer's 'you colored boys' speech
summary: After jokes about Jody, a small officer threatens the Black recruits, and Malachi prays to get out.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Plus, the first night that we went in the Navy, after we went through some kind of cleaning inspection -- that's what you go through when you first enter there... Then that night, we were in these barracks, and the barracks were all Black guys in there. And an incident happened that just made me almost convinced that something had to happen for me to get out of there. We had a bunch of new recruits, all of us. There must have been at least 50-100 of us in this particular
barracks. So, just having come off the street and everything, everybody's talking about what's happening, and guys kidding each other about what their old lady was doing back...
The guys were kidding each other, telling each other what their old lady's doing back home. And the guy who was left in the street, everybody referred to him as Jody, you know...!
Yeah. What it really meant was, they had an expression called "Joe, the Grinder." "Joe the Grinder's got your old lady!" But the short for that was Jody -- "Jody got your old lady." Just kiddin'!

So finally, this little guy comes in. He looks like he's probably 5'5", I guess. Small-built fellow, slight fellow. He's got on a uniform, and I don't know exactly what his position was, but he was an officer of some kind. He came in and said, "All right, you fellows. I want to welcome you to the Navy, so-and-so and so-and-so." Then he went on to break it down to what you were doing, and he said, "These lights go out at 8 o'clock, and you're supposed to go to sleep. There's going to be no activity in here afterwards," etcetera. Everybody's quiet and listening. You know this is really your
feeling of being in the Service, and he's running this speech down.

Anyway, he split, and I guess it must have been about a half-hour or 45 minutes before bedtime. So the guys... This really meant that you start getting undressed and everything. So anyway, sure enough, at 8 o'clock the lights went out, and the guys are laying up there in these bunks. So somebody makes a crack about something, everybody else laughs, and somebody else says something. Finally, the guys are buzzin' and they're talking and talking and talking. So somebody would say something else funny... And you know, the guys are talking!

So all of a sudden, the lights came on bright, and this, this little guy is standing up there with his legs spread apart and his hands on his hips. And he pointed his finger and said, "All right, you colored boys, you all knock that shit off in here. If I have to come back in here again, I'm going to run you all around the drill field in your shorts." Now, it's June in Great Lakes. June in Great Lakes is like February or March! You know, it's cold up there. It doesn't start to get warm up there until July or something. So boy, everybody's saying... This guy is saying "You colored boys" -- that really put a thing on us. "What is this?" So I'm laying up there, and I really prayed that night. I said, "Look, I've
got to come out of this thing some kind of way. I'm coming out dead or alive!"
